transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05 14:00 PT
Duration: ~75 min
Location: Zoom - Field Enablement Lab
Attendees: Jordan (AE), Priya (SE), Marco (SE), Ava (Ops) + Sam, Lina, Tom, Evelyn from Northstar field team

Summary:
Short: Internal hands-on enablement to align messaging vs competition, practice live demo transitions (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and workshop objection scripts. Focus on three demo flows: quick POC pitch, cost-sensitive enterprise pitch, and private/VPC pitch.

Topics covered:
- Messaging hooks (PLG vs enterprise)
- Demo flow transitions and checkpoint questions
- Competitive framing (Anthropic/OpenAI/Vertex)
- Live demo run-throughs with intentional interruptions
- Field objections and canned rebuttals
- Quick tech refresher (KV cache, batching, low-precision quantization tradeoffs)

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Jordan: All right folks, let's kick off. Thanks for carving out lab time. Quick round who wants to observe vs play?
[00:00:12] Sam: "I'll play AE first, Lina and Tom will watch, I'm mostly focused on the cost objection flow."
[00:00:18] Priya: Cool — we'll run the three flows in about 20 minute chunks, short feedback after each. We're intentionally adding interruptions to simulate real prospects.
[00:00:30] Marco: And I'm the designated troll today, I'm gonna ask the weird questions like "why not just host on k8s" — try to make rebuttals concise.
[00:00:38] Lina: Heads up, Northstar often hears "we can self host cheaper" so we want tight cost comparators.
[00:00:42] Jordan: Great. First, the opener we practiced — 30 seconds: product + one-liner + cost signal. Sam, you want to try?
[00:00:51] Sam: Yeah. "Hi, I'm Sam with Northstar — we help product teams ship LLM features faster. Redwood Inference gives consistent latency and drop-in routing so you don't have to build a bunch of ops, and we usually end up cheaper at scale because of batching and caching".
[00:01:10] (murmurs)
[00:01:12] Priya: Quick note: swap "we usually" for a stronger metric if available. Jordan, maybe mention the Dedicated SLA for enterprise calls.
[00:01:20] Jordan: Right. Suggestion: "...and you can get a 40% per-token reduction with KV caching and optimized batching for typical query shapes" — sample percent is rhetorical, but helps.
[00:01:32] Tom: Be careful with exact numbers unless you have the benchmark; we get asked for backup.
[00:01:36] Jordan: Good call. For field, use ranges and offer to follow up with the benchmark sheet.
[00:01:40] 
[00:02:05] (Live demo start)
[00:02:10] Sam (AE role): Okay, switching into demo. I'll start on hosted API — quick prompt, show streaming, then escalate to Dedicated for throughput.
[00:02:20] Priya (describing demo steps): Share screen -> show Playground -> run a sample chat with streaming -> point out latency metrics on top-right -> then show routing policy switch to Dedicated node pool.
[00:02:36] (screen share lag, someone coughs)
[00:02:45] Marco (interrupt): Wait what is that "routing policy" again? Is it per-route?
[00:02:50] Priya: Yes, routing policy can be per-route and you can set it by tag, region or SLA tier. For example pin generation-heavy routes to Dedicated and fallback to hosted variants.
[00:03:01] Sam (running sample): The streamed response looks clean but the prospect asks "why would you route away from the cheapest variant when under load?"
[00:03:12] Jordan: Pivot: emphasize latency SLOs and graceful degradation. "We route based on policy: if latency will be violated, we fallback to a compatible cheaper model only for non-critical paths".
[00:03:26] Lina: Small note, sometimes field hears "cheaper model" and thinks quality drops, so we should include a quick quality-check phrase.
[00:03:35] Priya: Suggested phrase: "We run an A/B safety filter that compares outputs across variants on edge cases before fallback." Could be too technical, but works for technical buyers.
[00:03:46] 
[00:04:20] (Demo glitch — model selection UI shows odd label)
[00:04:23] Jordan: Oh, looks like an ambiguous model alias — speak-up when the UI mislabels, call it out as "aliasing in the catalog, we'll map it in the deck"
[00:04:31] Marco: (mimics prospect) "We run LLMs ourselves on GKE, why pay you?"
[00:04:36] Priya: Rebuttal attempt: "If you already have full infra and ops, great — Redwood's play is to reduce unit cost and ops burden for application teams. Typical customers get better developer velocity and fewer outages because we maintain tuned kernels and KV cache consistency across versions."
[00:04:55] Tom: Ask the follow-up: "How do you handle secret management?" That's usually a compliance question.
[00:04:59] Priya: Answer: "We integrate KMS/HSM, provide audit logs, and for Private deployments we can run in your VPC with customer-managed keys."
[00:05:10] Jordan: Add the sales point: "For compliance-bound customers we recommend Private + dedicated routing and give an enterprise onboarding window."
[00:05:18] 
[00:06:00] (Switch to cost-sensitive flow)
[00:06:05] Sam: Prospect: "Your hosted price is X, we can get GPUs cheaper — what gives?"
[00:06:11] Marco: Rebuttal framework: 1) unit economics (per-token after batching/caching), 2) reliability & fallbacks cost, 3) time-to-ship. Offer to show a quick TCO spreadsheet later.
[00:06:25] Jordan: Good. Also raise example: "For high-qps embedding pipelines we often suggest quantized models + batching which reduces TCO by Y compared to naive hosting" (Y left intentionally vague in-surface).
[00:06:40] Lina: Field feedback: need a one-pager with sample numbers per workload (chat vs embeddings) — they'll ask for it on calls.
[00:06:46] Ava: I'll take that as an action, compile a 1-pager and reference benchmark.
[00:06:50] 
[00:10:12] (Technical pause — Priya does a mini-refresher)
[00:10:15] Priya: Quick tech refresher: KV cache helps with prefix reuse across sessions, prefix caching is more brittle but simpler. Batch windows are workload sensitive — too large and you hurt latency; too small and you lose cost benefits. Quantization options (8-bit, 4-bit) affect quality; use eval suite to measure degradation.
[00:10:40] Marco: Also flag that kernel selection matters on NPUs vs NVidia GPUs — when customers ask about hardware, keep it high level: we optimize kernels automatically.
[00:10:50] Sam: Write that down — customers will ask about "did you tune kernels for our sequence lengths".
[00:10:55] Priya: Short script: "We profile your trace to pick kernels & quant profiles; we present tradeoffs and pick an SLO-aligned config."
[00:11:04] 
[00:12:00] (Live roleplay run #2: Private/VPC pitch)
[00:12:05] Lina (AE): Opening: "For regulated data we offer Private deployments with customer-managed network, KMS integration, and audit-grade logs".
[00:12:20] Tom (prospect): "Can you do air-gapped?"
[00:12:23] Priya: "Short answer yes for on-prem package; longer answer is engagement with infra team and up-front ops runbook."
[00:12:29] Jordan: Add the sales nugget: "We recommend a two-week pilot with a reduced dataset to validate latency and logging before scaling".
[00:12:35] Tom: Good, that's practical.
[00:12:42] 
[00:15:00] (Feedback loop)
[00:15:05] Marco: Field pro-tip: when a prospect uses "we'll just self-host", don't immediately argue cost. Ask about SLAs, incident history, and who owns the LLM infra team.
[00:15:18] Sam: Good framing. It surfaces risk and org ownership.
[00:15:23] Lina: Also call out migration friction: matrix of model availability, latency, log retention.
[00:15:27] 
[00:20:00] (Second half: focused practice on objection handling + short cold open alternatives)
[00:20:05] Jordan: We'll test two alternate openers — A: Product velocity focus; B: Cost & reliability focus. Marco will roleplay a skeptical buyer.
[00:20:18] (Roleplay)
[00:20:25] Sam (opener A): "Many teams get blocks shipping LLM features because infra is complex — Redwood gives a single API and removes that block."
[00:20:33] Marco (cuts in): "Prove it. How long to go from idea to prod?"
[00:20:37] Sam: "Usually 2-4 weeks for a minimal feature with our SDKs and templates; we support more complex rollouts in 6-8 weeks."
[00:20:45] Priya: Note: avoid absolute weeks if you don't have an SOW; say 'typically' and offer a follow-up.
[00:20:53] Jordan: Strong. Also mention our quickstarts and sample templates.
[00:21:02] 
[00:24:00] (Nine minute dry-run of a full 7-minute demo)
[00:24:05] (Interruption: patchiness)
[00:24:12] Marco: (fonts a question) "What about eval regressions when you roll a new model?"
[00:24:16] Priya: "We tie quality monitoring to prompt sets and can auto-roll back if regressions appear — Redwood Optimize flags regressions against baseline prompts."
[00:24:30] Sam: Is that in the public docs?
[00:24:33] Jordan: Yes, but it's also a great leave-behind — we'll make sure to link it post-call. Action: Jordan share Optimize one-pager.
[00:24:40] 
[00:30:00] (Wrap-up and meta coaching)
[00:30:05] Priya: Coaching tips — keep rebuttals < 30s, always ask a follow-up question that surfaces org ownership, and use a one-liner that ties to buyer's persona (platform vs product).
[00:30:20] Marco: Script example: "If you own infra, what's your existing alerting and ops cadence for model drift?"
[00:30:27] Sam: That surfaces the ops gap well.
[00:30:40] Ava: Logistics — I'll publish the deck with the three demo flows and record this session. Also will add the shared spreadsheet with tuned numbers.
[00:30:50] Jordan: Final recap — who owns what?
[00:30:55] Ava: I'll publish draft 1-pager and benchmark ref by 11/06.
[00:31:02] Jordan: I'll share revised demo script + 2 openers by 11/07.
[00:31:06] Priya: I'll upload the benchmark spreadsheet and short KV-cache vs prefix note by 11/10.
[00:31:12] Marco: I'll drop the objection-rebuttal doc by 11/09.
[00:31:18] Lina: Can we schedule the dry-run with Sam and Lina for 11/11?
[00:31:22] Sam: Works for me.
[00:31:24] Jordan: Great. Any final questions?
[00:31:30] Evelyn: None here. Thanks — this was useful.
[00:31:34] Jordan: Thanks everyone, lab adjourned.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms — e.g., "kayv cache" noted in auto transcript as 'kayv' instead of KV; model names were abbreviated by field reps; timestamps approximate.
